Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 7595 (Part III) -1977 

Indian Standard 

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR OTTER BOARDS 

PART III OVAL OTTER BOARDS 
0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part III ) was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 29 July 1977, after the draft finalized by the Fishing 
Vessels Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo 
Movement and Packaging Division Council. 

0.2 This Standard is Part III in the series on otter boards, Part I and 
Part II cover general requirements of flat rectangular otter boards and 
rectangular horizontally curved otter boards respectively. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard ( Part III ) deals with the materials and general require- 
ments of oval otter boards. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 7595 
( Part I )-1975* shall apply, 

3. MATERIALS 

3.1 Name of Part Material Conforming to 

Otter board IS : 399-1963| 

Bracket IS : 2073-1970+ 

Back strop IS : 5537-1970§ or 

IS: 2266-1970|| 



♦General requirements for otter boards: Part I Flat rectangular otter boards. 
■^Classification of commerical timbers and their zonal distribution ( revised). 
JSpecification for carbon steel black bars for production of machined parts for general 
engineering purposes (first revision ). 
§Specification for lashing chains. 
([Specification for steel wire ropes for general engineering purposes (first revision ), 



IS: 7595 ( Part III )- 1977 

Name of Part Material Conforming to 

Kelly's eye IS : 2073-1970* 

Figure of 8-link IS : 2073-1970* 

Sole (shoe) IS : 5986-1970f 

Fittings IS : 5986-1970f 

Chain bridle IS : 5537-1970+ 

4. CONSTRUCTION 

4.1 The constructional details of oval otter board complete with fittings are 
shown in Fig. 1. The sides of the board shall be strengthened by mild steel 
sheet and the bottom part shall be filled with cement and iron pieces. 

4.2 For protection against corrosion, all metal parts shall be painted with 
a paint conforming to IS : 1404-1970§. 

5. DIMENSIONS 

5.1 The length and width of an otter board shall preferably be in a ratio 
of 1*6: 1. 

5.2 Brackets 

5.2.1 The fore bracket shall be fixed and the rear bracket shall be of 
adjustable chain bridle, fixed at distances of 22*5 percent and 39 percent 
of the total length of the otter board respectively from the fore and rear 
edges of the board. 

5.2.2 The brackets should be positioned at the symmetry axis of the 
board and their apex should fall approximately at 40 percent of board 
length from the fore edge. 

5.3 Rings — The fittings for rings on the outer side of the board for 
connecting the back strop shall be approximately at 20 percent of the length 
of the board from the rear edge of board. 



♦Specification for carbon steel black bars for production of machined parts for general 
engineering purposes {first revision ). 

fSpecification for hot-rolled steel plates and flats for cold-forming and flanging 
operations. 

^Specification for lashing chains. 

^Specification for anti-corrosive paint, brushing, for ships' bottoms and hulls ? red, 
chocolate or black, as required (first revision ).

5.4 Back Strop — The length of the back strop and bridle shall be as 
agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser (see Fig. 2 ). 

5.5 Shear Angle — Shear angle for oval otter boards ranging between 30° 
and 40° is considered most suitable.
